item.description: Nathan Lyon is set to be dropped by Australia for their next Test match and the spin bowler has been accused in fresh ball tampering accusations in the aftermath of Sandpapergate . Reports emerged that the 39-year-old spinner is set to be dropped when the squad for next month’s first Test against New Zealand is announced on Saturday. Having previously been squeezed out of the first XI on several occasions recently, he is now tipped to lose his squad place to Corey Rocchiccioli. Lyon is the sixth leading wicket-taker of all time with 577 wickets and had worked hard to recover from a hamstring injury last summer in order to return to the Test side. The news comes as Code Sports alleged Lyon was the previously unnamed player who suggested using mints to shine the ball against Pakistan in the first match after South Africa only to be angrily shot down by new head coach Justin Langer. Lyon has yet to respond publicly. item.description: FBL-EUR-C3-OLYMPIACOS-MILAN - AFP AC Milan manager Ruben Amorim was forced to issue a formal apology following a heated conclusion to his side's Europa League victory in Greece. The Portuguese coach addressed the friction caused by winger Diego Moreira, whose defiant actions overshadowed a brilliant rossoneri comeback. Amorim addresses Moreira’s controversial conduct Amorim found himself playing the role of peacemaker following Milan’s 4-2 victory over Olympiacos on Thursday night. The match ended in a state of high tension after Moreira, who scored the final goal to secure the win, celebrated in a way that deeply offended the home supporters and the Greek side's technical staff. The winger stood motionless, staring down the stands for several seconds in a gesture viewed as an intentional provocation. The young winger's actions immediately sparked a confrontation on the pitch, with Olympiacos players Jota Silva and Saliakas rushing to challenge the Milan man. item.title: 'I don't like it!' - Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho shuts down Zinedine Zidane comparisons after Jude Bellingham's Champions League masterclass
item.description: Real Madrid C.F. v PSV Eindhoven - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Jose Mourinho has shut down comparisons between Jude Bellingham and Zinedine Zidane following Real Madrid's emphatic 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven. The Portuguese manager addressed the growing hype during Friday's press conference, offering a measured verdict on how the two midfield greats should be viewed. Mourinho shuts down Zidane comparisons Mourinho has distanced himself from the growing debate linking Bellingham to Zidane. The comparisons surfaced earlier this week after the England midfielder delivered a standout display in Europe. Bellingham drew widespread acclaim following Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League triumph over PSV. His commanding performance prompted observers to draw parallels with the legendary French playmaker. However, when asked about the link during his media duties on Friday, Mourinho made it clear he has no interest in pitting the two players against each other. Different eras, same elite status Rather than weighing one midfielder's qualities against the other, the Portuguese tactician stressed that both players deserve to be judged strictly within their own eras. Mourinho believes generational gaps make direct comparisons pointless. "I don't like comparing footballers from different generations," Mourinho told reporters on Friday. "Zidane was one of the best of his generation and Jude is already one of the best of his." Bellingham's impressive numbers and humble view The praise surrounding Bellingham has been fuelled by his consistent output throughout the current campaign. At just 23 years old, the midfielder has already registered seven goals in 18 appearances across all competitions for Madrid this season. His display in the five-goal rout of PSV only intensified the spotlight. Yet despite his rapid rise and growing influence in Madrid, the England international remains grounded about his place in football history. When previously confronted with the same comparisons, Bellingham himself played down the hype , insisting that Zidane was "much better" than him. Focus on Alaves Bellingham and his teammates are currently preparing to face Deportivo Alaves at the Santiago Bernabeu in their upcoming Liga fixture. The England international will look to contribute once again for Los Blancos as they aim to secure all three points in front of their home supporters. Madrid currently sit second in the league standings with 33 points from 13 matches - three points behind the league leaders, Barcelona.

item.description: ANALYSIS | This is why Werder Bremen is No.1 in northern Germany Werder Bremen is the best team in northern Germany. At least that is what was evident from last weekend’s Nordderby, when they successfully beat Hamburg 4–0 at the Weserstadion. Bremen did more than just win that game; they demonstrated their quality this season and their ability to maximise the potential of their players to become a highly efficient team. This is the issue: The underlying numbers, in this case expected goals (xG), indicate that the game was actually very close – not as one-sided as the result suggests. HSV even had 1.54 compared to Bremen’s 1.52 in front of xG, per Opta. So, being able to win by a four-goal margin despite losing on xG shows just how effective Bremen are as a team. Get German Football News’ Bergas investigates why… First thing first: Underlying numbers need context Yes, HSV has more numbers in front of xG. However, if we look at the xG data itself, 1.03 of HSV’s 1.54 came after they fell behind in the 55th minute. In this situation, the state of the game changed, with HSV adopting a more proactive approach with the ball. Meanwhile, between minutes 1 and 54, when the score was still 0–0, HSV only achieved an xG of 0.5 (Bremen had 0.84). This is why xG is not the best metric with which to measure HSV’s performance in this game, because the state of the game forced them to create more chances in order to catch up, resulting in lots of shots. In fact, however, they weren’t really dangerous enough to challenge or harm Bremen. Looking at other metrics such as key passes, HSV weren’t superior either during the even time when the score was still 0–0. In that period, they made four key passes compared to Bremen’s eight. HSV found it much harder to create shots than the home team. Even in the first half, when Bremen were underperforming in parts, HSV didn’t look particularly threatening. Bremen flexible defensive structure made HSV toothless One of the reasons for that is Bremen’s flexibility in their approach to HSV when defending. In the first half, they often used a man-to-man approach (which was more aggressive), which successfully forced HSV to use long balls to progress the ball to the final third, particularly on their left side. item.description: Liverpool make transfer decision ahead of January window Jeremie Frimpong Faces Big Liverpool Test Under Andoni Iraola Jeremie Frimpong’s first start in Liverpool’s 3-0 Champions League win over Club Brugge felt significant for more than the result. After an injury-hit spell and a stop-start first year at Anfield, the 25-year-old is trying to re-establish himself in a position that remains open, competitive and still under assessment. According to the Daily Mail, Frimpong has no desire to move on despite reported Saudi Arabia interest. His focus is on staying at Liverpool and proving himself to Andoni Iraola. That determination will matter, because the head coach has already shown he values intensity, direct running and aggressive full-back play, traits Frimpong naturally brings. Liverpool invested £29.5 million to sign him from Bayer Leverkusen, backing a player with a strong reputation in the Bundesliga and across Europe. Yet his first season on Merseyside never found full rhythm. Injury disruption and inconsistency limited his wider impact, with 35 appearances, two goals and two assists across all competitions. Photo: IMAGO Right-back battle remains open The broader picture adds intrigue. Conor Bradley has also endured fitness frustrations, while Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona and primarily a centre-back, has stepped in at right-back to strong effect. His displays have given Iraola a dependable option, one that appears to offer balance and reliability in and out of possession. That leaves Frimpong with a clear challenge. His attacking strengths are obvious, pace, width, energy and a willingness to drive Liverpool forward. He can stretch teams and create overloads, particularly when matches become open. Those qualities suit Iraola’s football. Defensive questions still need answering The concern is whether Frimpong can offer enough defensive control in a back four over a sustained period. Liverpool need a right-back who can recover quickly, protect space behind him and stay disciplined when the game turns. That part of the role will shape how Iraola judges him over the months ahead. Frimpong’s return has arrived at an important moment. He has the talent to become a valuable Liverpool option, and perhaps more than that, but the next phase is about trust. If he can show growth without the ball, this conversation shifts quickly. If he cannot, Liverpool may yet revisit the market. item.title: Eight-time champion Marquez to retire from MotoGP
item.description: Marc Marquez's eight MotoGP titles have come between 2013 and 2026 [Getty Images] MotoGP champion Marc Marquez has said he will retire days after clinching a record-equalling eighth title. The 33-year-old Spaniard clinched the 2026 world championship in Portugal last weekend, putting him level with Giacomo Agostini and one clear of modern great Valentino Rossi. The Ducati rider had extended his contract until 2028 in June but will now end his professional career after the final race of the season in Valencia on Sunday. "Thank you to everyone who's been part of the journey," he said. "I hope you've enjoyed it as much as I have." Marquez won his first title in 2013 and remains the only rider to win a MotoGP championship in his rookie year. He began his MotoGP career with Honda, winning six titles in seven seasons up to 2019. After joining Gresini Racing - the satellite Ducati team - for 2024, he spent the past two seasons with the Italian outfit's factory team - winning the championship in both. "It is official," read a team statement. "Marc Marquez has decided to retire from MotoGP, and the 2026 Valencia Grand Prix will be his final race as a professional rider and with the Ducati Lenovo team." item.title: 'That's his problem!' - Vinicius Jr handed blunt reality check by Jose Mourinho as Real Madrid boss demands collective sacrifice ahead of Alaves clash
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-REAL MADRID-INTER MILAN - AFP Jose Mourinho has sent a clear message to Vinicius Jr and the rest of his Real Madrid stars, insisting that individual reputations mean nothing compared to the needs of the collective. Speaking ahead of the clash with Alaves, the Portuguese coach made it clear that even the biggest names at the Bernabeu must accept their role for the good of the team. Mourinho dismisses guaranteed starting spots The 'Special One' has rejected the idea of a fixed starting line-up at Real Madrid ahead of Saturday night’s La Liga clash against Deportivo Alaves. Addressing the media, the Portuguese coach faced repeated questions over whether Vinicius Jr has done enough to reclaim a regular berth. Mourinho insisted recent speculation around Vinicius’s future and his compatibility with Real's record signing Yan Diomande carries no weight inside the club. While acknowledging the Brazilian has improved, he stressed that team unity always overrides individual standing. 'That's his problem!' Asked how Vinicius compares to Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham - with Bellingham benched only once this season - Mourinho delivered a blunt verdict, attributing their heavy involvement strictly to superior displays. "That’s his problem, not mine," Mourinho said of Vinicius's place in the side. "Mbappe and Bellingham are on the same level as everyone else. If they end up on the bench someday… that’s just how it is. The collective goal is above the individual. The difference lies in their incomparable performance compared to the rest." He also dismissed hints of rivalry between Vinicius and Diomande after their recent celebrations together: "It’s not about competition, we’re all together and we all want the same thing. We’re achieving stability and it seems your objective is to create this doubt. Nobody on the team wants that." Squad depth and unity driving Madrid's resurgence Over his five months in charge, Mourinho has built a steady environment that contrasts with last season’s dressing-room problems. That depth showed when Thibaut Courtois missed his only game through illness, allowing Andriy Lunin to step in and prove decisive. "We have been together for five months and we haven’t had any issues," Mourinho explained. "People want to play; nobody likes being left out or not getting minutes. The collective objective will overcome any individual egos." Title pressure mounts as transfer stance becomes clear Beating Alaves on Saturday will seal an 11th straight win across all competitions for Los Blancos, who have won every match since the first international break and thrashed PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League this week. Victory will also pile pressure on La Liga leaders Barcelona, who sit three points ahead before playing on Sunday. With two months left until the transfer window opens, Mourinho also shut down squad exit or arrival talk: "I don’t want anyone coming in and out. I don’t want any transfer rumours."

item.title: Argyle's fit-again Oseni making up for lost time
item.description: Owen Oseni has featured as a substitute in Plymouth's past two League One games [Shutterstock] Plymouth Argyle striker Owen Oseni hopes he can re-establish himself in the side after returning to full fitness. The 23-year-old, who won his first cap for Nigeria over the summer, has recovered from an ankle injury he suffered in late September. At that time, he had only just returned to fitness after injuring his thigh late in pre-season. "It was devastating for me, for my support system, for my family," he told BBC Radio Devon. "It's all part of the game but I don't think I've ever experienced this side of the game, picking up two injuries in such quick succession. "So it was good to learn, just experience that part of the game and just make sure I stay focused, I do my work in the gym and try to come back as quick as I can to help the lads." Plymouth Argyle striker Oseni suffers injury blow Plymouth target attacking signing after Oseni injury Plymouth striker Oseni makes Nigeria debut Oseni has not started a league game since Argyle's 2-2 draw with Exeter City in April. His only starts since then have come in the Jersey Mike's Trophy - he was injured in the 5-1 win over Crystal Palace Under-21s in September before returning in the win over Swindon Town earlier this month. But with Will Evans suspended and fellow forward Bim Pepple also returning to fitness, Oseni has the chance to impress when Argyle travel to Wigan Athletic on Saturday, having featured from the bench in the past two matches. "Owen has been training well this week, been really clean in training, looks fitter and fitter," head coach Tom Cleverley said. item.title: Will Stein explains his decision to not call plays for Kentucky Football
item.description: Will Stein’s debut season as a head coach has been a success. The last three games have brought some negativity within the fanbase, but overall, and especially if you can go win the Governor’s Cup to get your eighth win of the season, it’s a successful year one. Stein took over a program with a difficult schedule and not a ton of pieces returning, and entered the year with a betting over/under of 4.5 wins, and got the over on that on October 10 when Kentucky stunned LSU in its second straight victory after beating South Carolina in the same fashion a week earlier. Well, going into the season, there was one decision Stein made that turned some heads and brought some questioning. He said he wouldn’t be calling the offense and that he wants to be a great head coach rather than just an offensive mind. Now, he did mention it’ll have his input, and he won’t abandon it completely, but he would allow the offensive play-calling to be done by former LSU offensive coordinator Joe Sloan. Why is that? Well, Stein answered that with a detailed explanation this week. “I think as a competitor, you want to be in that spot,” Stein said. “But I know for the good of the entire organization, not just the on-the-field play, but recruiting, sports strength and conditioning, our training room, nutrition, fundraising, everything that embodies being a head coach in today’s college football, it was important for me to be at my best for the entirety of the organization. “What we do on Saturdays is really a collection of everybody in our offensive staff room, defensive staff room, special teams room, and using that collaboration and the brain power that we have to formulate the best possible plan that we feel like can go win a football game. And just because I’m not saying it over the mic to the quarterback doesn’t mean that I don’t have my hands in those decisions. “I feel like Joe Sloan has done a fantastic job this season. We’ve battled through ups and downs and adversity. And what I love about Joe is his confidence, his ability to communicate, his ability to connect with players.” Stein then added more on Sloan, saying, “The confidence that he gives our players and our team is really special. And so I’ve been very proud of him and developing this relationship that we have here at Kentucky together.” Stein certainly acknowledged the dip in scoring production in the last three contests after scoring only six against Tennessee, 14 against Florida, and 14 at Missouri, but shows some excitement in the potential of the offense in Saturday’s game against Louisville and onto the postseason. So far, it’s been a success to have Sloan call the plays, with a little bit of Stein’s input during game-planning. Let’s hope this offense can find a way to take care of it, score the ball, and get back to the way it showed earlier in the season.

item.title: ‘He has come back with a different attitude’ – Filipe Luís pays tribute to Monaco forward Folarin Balogun
item.description: ‘He has come back with a different attitude’ – Filipe Luís pays tribute to Monaco forward Folarin Balogun Filipe Luís has paid tribute to Folarin Balogun’s (25) attitude since returning from the most recent international break. The USMNT forward netted a brace as AS Monaco beat Hearts in the UEFA Conference League on Thursday night. Paris Brunner missed the game in Scotland due to a muscular injury, so it was a chance for Balogun to re-establish himself at Monaco. The former Arsenal man missed the start of the season due to injury and his summer was also marked by the episode of his failed move to Everton. Since returning to fitness, Balogun has failed to replicate the kind of form that saw him become the subject of a €50m approach from Everton. Speaking last week, Filipe Luís evoked the American’s situation: “ For me, it’s very simple. Monaco is bigger than any player. It’s bigger than everybody. And I want players who want to be here, of course. And I need Balogun to feel that he belongs here, that he wants to play here, because then if he plays, he scores goals; it’s going to be easier to make him fulfil his objective .” Just days before, Balogun had reaffirmed his ambition to leave Monaco in the near future. Luís has now praised the forward, who he says has returned from this month’s international break “with a different attitude.” ”He had a summer that was difficult to come to terms with , like Lamine Camara, who was also close to leaving. It is difficult to experience, especially after having played in the World Cup and having heard so many rumours in the press. That also explains why he found it difficult to come back. “Since he came back in November, he has really come back with a different attitude. He is a super player who could still leave in January but until then, he is still a Monaco player and I hope that I will still be able to benefit from him,” said Luís after his brace in the win over Hearts (2-3). item.title: Cricket Australia gives players six weeks to share accounts of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
item.description: Cricket Australia (CA) has made public the terms of reference for its independent forum examining the events surrounding the controversial 2018 South Africa tour, which became infamous for the ball-tampering scandal. The six-week exercise will give players and support staff who were part of the tour an opportunity to share their experiences, although individual accounts will remain confidential and will not be made available to the CA Board. The board will instead receive a report summarising the key issues raised during the process, along with recommendations. The document will not include individual testimonies or any supporting material. CA has also committed to releasing the complete report, together with its response, within 30 days of receiving it. The independent exercise will be overseen by senior counsel Fiona McLeod AO SC, who will conduct private sessions with those willing to participate. The forum was announced following fresh revelations surrounding the 2018 scandal in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr . In the book, Khawaja claimed that awareness of the sandpaper plan extended beyond the three players who were sanctioned by CA. David Warner and Cameron Bancroft have supported parts of his account, while Pat Cummins and several other bowlers have maintained that they had no knowledge of the plan. The forum will examine Australia's ball-management practices during the 2017-18 season, the team's involvement in all four Tests of the South Africa tour, and the incident involving Bancroft during the third Test in Cape Town on March 24, 2018. It will also look into CA's subsequent investigation into the episode. However, the exercise is not intended to reopen the original investigation or establish individual responsibility for the incident. CA has extended invitations to all players and support staff who were part of the South Africa tour, along with the management officials and board directors who were associated with the organisation at the time. Participants will be able to share their accounts through face-to-face or online meetings with McLeod, submit written statements or provide relevant documents. Taking part in the process is voluntary, and those who choose to participate will be permitted to have a support person or legal representative present. item.title: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.”
item.description: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.” The strength of Hoffenheim’s bench proved decisive in Thursday evening’s 3-1 Europa League comeback victory over Sturm Graz. Christian Ilzer’s substitutes supplied two of the three goals as the Kraichgauer recovered from a disappointing first half to secure an important European victory against their head coach’s former club. Hoffenheim entered the dressing room trailing 1-0 after Oumar Diakité’s 43rd-minute opener, with sections of the home crowd expressing their displeasure at the halftime whistle. The hosts nevertheless emerged with renewed energy and eventually turned the match around. Speaking to journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Austrian international Alexander Prass insisted that Hoffenheim’s response had not surprised him. “No it doesn’t surprise me,” Prass remarked in the mixed zone when questioned about the comeback. “Because we’re just a really awesome crew. We’re capable of banding together even after a total shit first half, or a not so good first half. Sorry. We can up the energy. Every individual can help us mutually bring what was lacking in the first half. We did everything better in the second half.” Hoffenheim’s substitutes deliver decisive contributions Ilzer’s decision to introduce Patrick Wimmer, Andrej Kramaric, and Bambasé Conté shortly after the hour mark proved particularly influential. Adam Hlozek equalized in the 72nd minute before Conté completed the turnaround eight minutes later, finishing off a Tim Lemperle cross. Substitute Max Moerstedt sealed the 3-1 victory with his first touch in the 90th minute. Wimmer initiated the attack by winning possession, with Kramaric subsequently setting up the young German striker. Conté, himself one of the decisive substitutes, agreed when asked about the quality of Hoffenheim’s options from the bench. “Yeah you could say that,” Conté responded in the mixed zone. “We made it difficult for ourselves in the first half. From the restart onwards we produced a very positive energy with the substitutions and we turned the game around.” Hoffenheim have already benefited from influential substitute appearances this season. As GGFN examined following the club’s 3-0 Bundesliga victory over Bayer Leverkusen , Kramaric also transformed that encounter after entering in the second half, contributing a goal and an assist. Despite Thursday’s successful turnaround, team captain Oliver Baumann was less inclined to celebrate the performance unreservedly. Speaking to RTL after the match, the goalkeeper criticized Hoffenheim’s first-half approach and stressed that the team must learn to sustain its improved football over 70 or 80 minutes rather than relying on one good half. item.description: Motorsport photo Marco Bezzecchi set the pace in the opening practice for the Valencia Grand Prix, leading the soon-to-be-retiring Marc Marquez. One particular incident raised eyebrows when Hattab showed a yellow card to Al Jazira’s goalkeeper for a foul that happened close to the halfway line, 40 yards away from him. Hattab was then replaced at half-time with the fourth official taking over for the remainder of the game, which Al Jazira won 1-0. Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following erratic decision-making as similar accusations flooded in online. item.title: Shaquille O’Neal thinks Anthony Edwards can ruin Timberwolves if he fails to notice one thing
item.description: Credit: Marcin Golba/NurPhoto/David Berding via Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves have been doing quite well even without Anthony Edwards, and Shaquille O’Neal has sent the superstar a warning about his eventual return. Anthony Edwards has been out indefinitely since he had arthroscopic surgery on his right knee late in October. The Minnesota Timberwolves superstar has missed the entirety of November, and will likely miss all of December and a fair amount of time in January as well. The Timberwolves haven’t struggled all that much in his absence, either. LaMelo Ball has fit the team like a glove, and they have a 14-5 record going into Friday’s game against the Memphis Grizzlies. With that in mind, Shaquille O’Neal recently shared some advice for the young superstar for when he does return. Shaquille O’Neal says Anthony Edwards will have to ensure he doesn’t disrupt team rhythm after returning The Timberwolves have played excellent team ball in Edwards’ absence. He was averaging over 33 points per game in his four games this season. Since he’s been out, though, the team has five players averaging between 12 points to 19 points per game. No one star has been dominating, and this style has been working quite well. So Shaq thinks Edwards will have to be careful with that when he does come back. “I think it’s going to be up to Anthony Edwards,” O’Neal said. “Because right now, he has to see how the guys are playing. item.description: Barcelona injury crisis raises alarm across men’s and women’s teams and Barça Atlètic Barcelona are facing growing concern over an injury crisis affecting several sections of the club, with the men’s and women’s first teams, Barça Atlètic and even the basketball side all struggling with player absences, according to a report from SPORT . The mounting problems have intensified fears that an increasingly congested calendar is taking a physical toll on the club’s athletes across all the divisions. Despite investment in medical staff, rehabilitation support and injury prevention, Barcelona have yet to find a solution to the growing number of setbacks. The situation is particularly troubling for the football department, where Hansi Flick’s first team has repeatedly been forced to manage injuries during demanding stretches of the season. Unfortunately, however, the concern is not limited to the senior squad, with the reserve team also experiencing a difficult run. A packed calendar is testing Barcelona’s prevention work Hansi Flick strengthened the first-team physical preparation staff in July by bringing in Benjamin Kugel , aiming to improve conditioning and reduce late-season injury problems. Hansi Flick has been dealing with player shortages, especially in defence, this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Yet muscle injuries remain a recurring issue amid international travel and matches every three or four days. Specifically, the stretch involving Betis, Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid illustrated the cost. Eric García, Jules Kounde, Xavi Espart and Dani Olmo suffered injuries during that period, while Gerard Martin also experienced discomfort . The sequence left Flick managing absences during a demanding run of fixtures. Barça Atlètic faces the most severe shortage The reserve team has been hit especially hard. Before facing Girona B, Juliano Belletti was dealing with a shortage caused by injuries and international call-ups, with reports counting more than 20 unavailable players. Barcelona requested that the fixture be postponed, but it went ahead. Barcelona have suffered several injuries this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The match brought further damage, as Dani Avila and Ibrahim Diarra were injured , while other players finished with physical problems. Barça Atlètic subsequently lost Mirza Catovic in the derby against Espanyol B. Barcelona confirmed that Catovic had suffered a fibula fracture and would be out for around four months, taking the reserve side’s injury list to 12. Unfortunately, Barcelona’s women’s side is also dealing with a difficult injury situation, while the basketball team has been managing absences during a packed domestic and EuroLeague schedule. The pattern across several departments makes the issue bigger than an isolated run of bad luck. Barcelona have invested in prevention and recovery, but workload, travel and limited rest continue to challenge those measures.

item.title: Ex-Patriots quarterback Joe Milton steals the show on Thanksgiving
item.description: With one former New England Patriots quarterback in the broadcast booth, another played the game of his life. Joe Milton, under the watchful eye of Tom Brady, led the Philadelphia Eagles to a 39-38 road victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. And even on a day that saw the likes of Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, Caleb Williams, Jared Goff and Dak Prescott all line up under center, it was the third-year QB that stole the show. Milton completed 21 of 31 pass attempts for 331 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He also led the game-winning drive when he marched Philadelphia’s offense into kicker Jake Elliott’s field goal range in the late fourth quarter, helping the Eagles overcome what was a 21-point deficit in the late third quarter. In addition, he proved why his “Bazooka Joe” nickname was well earned: he threw some truly spectacular passes. Every time Joe Milton made the craziest throw of the year vs the Cowboys 5 different times. pic.twitter.com/lVuL46DCmH — Cam (@42Cyc) November 27, 2026 Milton completed six of his 11 deep pass attempts versus the Cowboys, gaining 188 yards and scoring three touchdowns. He finished the game with 0.308 expected points added per play, a completion percentage 12.1 points over expectation, and an average of 17.3 air yards — ranking first among all six of the quarterbacks taking the field on Thursday. Whether he can build on the successful outing in front of a national audience will be seen. For Milton, however, it was a high point on what had been a rollercoaster of a career so far. That rollercoaster, of course, that started when the Patriots selected him in the sixth round of the 2024 draft. Milton was brought in in the same draft class as third overall pick Drake Maye, whose status as the Patriots’ future face of the franchise was never questioned. This, in turn, put his fellow then-rookie on a path to backup duty; but with veteran Jacoby Brissett also under contract at the time, not even that materialized. He ended up playing just one game as a rookie, the season finale against Buffalo a mere hours before head coach Jerod Mayo was fired. Milton completed 22 of 29 passes in that contest for 241 yards and a touchdown, leading New England to its fourth game of the year (and to drop out of the first overall draft pick). With a new regime under Mike Vrabel coming in, however, his days were numbered. In April of 2025, Milton and a seventh-round pick were sent to Dallas for a fifth-rounder. Through a series of follow-up trade, Patriots turned that selection into kicker Andy Borregales, long snapper Julian Ashby and cornerback Kobee Minor. Milton, meanwhile, played four games in his first season as a Cowboy but lost the QB2 competition this summer. He started his 2026 campaign on the Dallas practice squad, but was signed off of it by the Eagles in October. A month later, and with him now serving as Philadelphia’s starter in place of the injured Jalen Hurts, he now got the best of his former team.

item.title: Fabio Cannavaro reveals Liverpool star Virgil van Dijk's desire to play in Serie A amid AC Milan links
item.description: 버질 판데이크 (Virgil van Dijk) - Getty Images Fabio Cannavaro has revealed that Liverpool centre-back Virgil van Dijk expressed a desire to play in Serie A during a conversation at the World Cup. With the Dutchman's contract expiring in June 2027, the Italy legend believes a switch to AC Milan would be an exciting move. Van Dijk eyes Italian football adventure Liverpool could face a battle to keep hold of Van Dijk as speculation grows over his long-term future . The Dutch centre-back has reportedly emerged on Milan's radar ahead of next season. Former Italy international Cannavaro has now added fuel to those rumours in an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport . The 2006 Ballon d'Or winner disclosed that Van Dijk is genuinely intrigued by the prospect of testing himself in Italian football. Van Dijk existing deal with Liverpool is set to expire in June 2027, leaving the door open for potential suitors to monitor his availability. Cannavaro backs Dutchman for Milan switch Cannavaro explained that his insight came directly from a personal conversation with the Liverpool defender during the World Cup. Having represented Napoli, Parma, Juventus, and Inter during his own career, the Italian icon believes Milan would be a fitting destination. "I saw him at the World Cup and he told me that he would like to have an experience in Italy," Cannavaro said. "He is very fascinated by it. It would be nice to see Van Dijk at Milan." Physical dominance and the Maldini comparison While Cannavaro is clearly an admirer of Van Dijk's attributes, he also offered a candid tactical assessment of how elite defenders evolve over time. Drawing on his own experiences and an anecdote involving Paolo Maldini, Cannavaro highlighted the vital role of pace in defending. "In recent years, he has combined great physical strength with outstanding speed," Cannavaro noted. "Once, a coach said to Paolo Maldini: 'You turn badly.' And he replied: 'Mister, as long as I get to the ball.'" Cannavaro warned that relying on recovery speed comes with an inevitable caveat later in a player's career. "It was the same for me," he added. "When you are very fast, you can afford a technical error. The problem comes when that speed is no longer there." What next for Van Dijk's future? With Van Dijk's Liverpool contract running until June 2027, the club still hold a strong position regarding his immediate future. However, Milan's reported interest for next season means the Italian side could soon test Liverpool's resolve. Whether Van Dijk decides to act on his fascination with Serie A remains to be seen.

item.description: Newcastle United defender Sven Botman has been banned from driving [PA] Premier League footballer Sven Botman has been banned from driving after being caught using his mobile phone at the wheel. item.description: Fan violence marred the tie at the Stade Velodrome [Getty Images] Violent clashes marred a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French president Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia. There were also incidents at games between Turkish side Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia and Sunderland's 1-1 home draw with Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok. In Marseille, the build-up to the Europa League match at the Stade Velodrome was affected by incidents in the stands, including the throwing of projectiles and flares between the two sets of supporters. With 10 minutes to go until kick-off, several Marseille fans ran from a home stand, appearing to pursue a group of Levski Sofia supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, which housed around 500 supporters of the Bulgarian domestic champions. "Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," said the Marseille police prefecture. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds." Macron spoke to Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev about the incidents, with the French president condemning "with the utmost force these acts of violence, which have no place in sport or in public space", and reassured him that "these acts would not go unpunished". According to news agency Reuters, Radev thanked Macron for his personal involvement following the "attack on Bulgarian citizens" and for the medical assistance provided to the victims. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said she found video footage of the incidents "shocking" in a statement posted on social media. "The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she added. item.description: "I don't want to shut out the noise, we just need to know that it's coming and it's going to be electric." The "noise" Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert refers to has been building over recent weeks, with 'Spygate' returning to the collective consciousness as Saints and Middlesbrough meet on Friday (20:00 GMT) for the first time since the scandal. The most recent time they came face-to-face was in last season's Championship play-off semi-finals. item.title: Lucas Herbert claims he's 'owed a lot' of money from LIV Golf as he suggests whether he regrets joining the league
item.description: Photo by David Cannon/Getty Images LIV Golf officially applied for bankruptcy and began the process of going into liquidation earlier this month. Their plans for a new version of the league – LIV 2.0 – failed to get off the ground after they failed to get enough players to sign up to the project. After many years of bullish promises, LIV Golf is finally finished and the fallout from their collapse will be ongoing for quite some time. LIV Golf may have made a lot of big-name players incredibly wealthy initially, but a lot of golfers have been left in the lurch over the past 12 months regarding payments they’re due. However, it is tough to extract money from a business that has entered into bankruptcy. One golfer in particular is claiming that he is owed a lot of money from the former Saudi-backed league. Lucas Herbert claims he’s ‘owed a lot’ of money from LIV Golf The talented Lucas Herbert spoke with Fox Sports Australia about his recent exit from LIV Golf. The 30-year-old Australian claimed he’s still owed a lot of money from LIV, but suggested that he doesn’t regret his decision to join the league in the first place. “ You’re probably foolish to think you’re going to get much of it. Anything from this point is going to be a bonus, “ Herbert said. “ It’s a long drawn out process with mostly lawyers winning out of the whole battle. I’ve accepted that and moved on. The reality is I made a lot of money at the same time as I’m owed a lot. “ As great as a time I had on the LIV tour, I had many legal issues along the way, which drew a lot of energy out of me. I’ve played this game a few times now and I’m going to expect not very much and hopefully be pleasantly surprised, rather than the other way around. “ I’ve got no problem saying we were poorly communicated with as players throughout the season,” he said. “ A lot of times mainstream media, or media outlets outside of LIV, knew more about what was going on than we did, which was pretty tough to deal with. It was a bit of a contributing factor as to why very few guys were interested in going around again in 2.0. “ It was a tough off-season to have everyone having an opinion on what your livelihood and career and future looks like when you don’t have control over (it) yourself. It’s one thing for people to have their opinions on your poor play, but it felt people at times took pride in seeing everything we tried to build at LIV fail. “ I’m still very happy with the decision I made – it doesn’t look like I’m in a great position right now, but time will tell. “ Herbert is a sensational golfer, so he will undoubtedly make millions of dollars in the future. However, the fact that he is owed so much money from LIV Golf must really be eating away at him. No wonder none of the big names were keen to sign up to LIV 2.0 after being treated so poorly.

item.description: Ex-Man United ace Alejandro Garnacho left staring into the abyss after Aston Villa decision Former Manchester United forward Alejandro Garnacho has plunged to a new all-time low, with Aston Villa making a major decision on his future ahead of the January transfer window. Troubles Garnacho was nowhere to be seen on Tuesday evening as Villa suffered a 1-0 Champions League defeat to Galatasaray. Villa boss Unai Emery opted to name 11 substitutes instead of the allowed 12. Emery took the decision amid deepening concerns over the trajectory of Garnacho ‘s career. Since his £40m move from United to Chelsea in the summer of 2025, he has endured a torrid time, having departed after falling out with then-manager Ruben Amorim. He struggled both for form and consistency at Chelsea, managing just one Premier League goal all term. Chelsea decided they had seen enough and approved a move to Villa , initially on loan, with the deal set to become an obligation depending on appearances. But Garnacho has so far failed to impress Emery, both during games and on the training pitch. The Argentine has been omitted from the previous two Premier League squads and has accumulated only 34 minutes of top-flight football. He has made just seven appearances from the bench. According to The Athletic , Villa are actively working to offload the Carrington academy graduate in January. New low The Athletic reports, “Two Villa sources stated in October that they would be amazed if Garnacho did not end up their player beyond the season, with staff being briefed that the initial loan came with the extreme likelihood that Garnacho would transition into a permanent acquisition.” Alejandro Garnacho 2026/27 record Aston Villa · 2026/27 “Garnacho had wanted to leave England before meeting with Emery, who convinced him to stay. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
